issues.legal_issue: Compound interest accruing on unpaid interest is not deductible as interest on a capital charge when calculating income from property.
material_facts: The assessee was a trustee of house property subject to an obligation to pay an amount secured against the property, with interest at a specified annual rate.
A consent decree provided for compound interest, and unpaid interest was added to the amount on which further interest accrued.
For the relevant assessment years, the assessee claimed a deduction that included interest on the unpaid interest.
The tax authorities allowed a deduction only for interest calculated on the original outstanding capital amount, and the High Court upheld that treatment.
issues.conclusion: Only simple interest payable on the original capital charge was deductible; interest accruing on unpaid interest was not deductible.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9(1)(iv) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the allowable deduction is the amount of interest on the mortgage or other capital charge. Unpaid interest that becomes part of the amount on which further interest accrues does not thereby become a capital charge; further interest on it remains interest on interest. Treating that additional interest as deductible could allow a taxpayer to obtain a tax advantage from failing to pay interest when due, so that interpretation is impermissible. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

issues.definition: When a property-income deduction dispute involves a capital charge and the claimed deduction includes interest accruing on unpaid interest added to the interest-bearing amount, only interest on the original capital charge is deductible.
